scope: Independent security audit of F68 after the 13th evaluator judgment (pass, min-of-5 7, security 8, F37 cross-check agreeing). Per the dispatch brief this audit did not re-litigate criteria the evaluator passed; it targeted the residual items the judgment recorded but did not treat as fail reasons, and the round's file scope for regressions. All verdicts below are grounded in commands executed this session, in an isolated clone and on a purpose-built case-sensitive volume; no test wrote to the live repository.
scan_tools: differential hook harness (isolated git clone, synthetic PreToolUse payloads, OLD/NEW comparison)
live end-to-end probes through the real Claude Code Edit/Write tool chain
case-sensitive APFS volume (hdiutil) for the filesystem-dependent legs
bats 743 re-run independently in an isolated clone: 1..743, 743 ok, 0 failures, exit 0
jq structural diffing, git history secret scan
manual review of hooks/invariant-guard.sh, hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh, hooks/protected-integrity.sh

details: package.json declares no dependencies and no devDependencies; there is no package-lock.json and no node_modules. npm audit / govulncheck / dart pub outdated are not applicable — there is no dependency graph to audit.
Runtime dependencies are system binaries: bash, jq, awk, git, bats. The guard already fails closed when jq or awk is absent (hooks/invariant-guard.sh:151-163, :404-414).
engines.node >= 16 is declared but no JavaScript is executed by the harness; init.sh is a bash bootstrapper delivered through the npm bin entry.

secrets_scan.note: All matches for api_key/secret/token/private-key patterns in the last 20 commits are documentation prose about the firewall's own SECRET_PATHS arm, not credentials.

checklist_compliance.source: progress/contracts/sprint-54.json security_criteria (SC-1..SC-4) + docs/INVARIANTS.md (INV-1..INV-14). No docs/SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md exists in this repository; INVARIANTS.md is the operative checklist.
failed_items: SC-4 (무인 루프의 승인 범위 조작이 단일 쓰기로는 불가능하다) — violated on two independent paths, both measured. Structurally identical to the 6th judgment's `rm <contract>` + one Write, which was ruled an SC-4 violation: one firewall-allowed preparatory action plus one Write.

INV-13 (설치 경로 간 훅 배선은 대칭이다) — wiring files with no HEAD blob (.claude/settings.json, and any hooks.json outside the project root) can be deleted and recreated unwired with the guard returning exit 0, and nothing restores them.

verified: path spelling variants (//, ./, case-variant on a case-insensitive FS) — canon_file normalizes; verified live, a Write to tests/ZZ-PROBE.BATS was denied with the message naming the real spelling zz-probe.bats
directory symlink in the prefix — pwd -P resolves it

final-component symlink — verified live through the real tool: a Write to the symlink alias.bats was denied by the @test-count check on its target zz-probe.bats. Claude Code does NOT resolve symlinks before the hook, so this round's resolve_file_symlink is genuinely load-bearing
symlink cycle / depth cap exhausted — rc 1 then deny
mid-chain EACCES (immediate parent chmod 000) — rc 1 then deny, exit 2 measured; this is the leg the 13th round closed and it works
delete-then-recreate for HEAD-tracked in-repo files — HEAD materialization holds (hooks/hooks.json deleted then recreated unwired gives exit 2)
truncation by empty Write on an existing protected file — deny
gaps: canon_file's case-insensitive filename rebind is not gated on the filesystem actually being case-insensitive — on a case-sensitive FS a decoy file redirects the guard's judgment to a different real file (F-2)
delete-then-recreate remains open for control-plane files with no HEAD blob: .claude/settings.json (gitignored) and any wiring file outside the project root (F-1)
canon_file returns the raw path when it cannot enter the parent directory instead of failing closed (F-3)
grandparent-and-above directory inaccessibility still conflates 'cannot judge' with 'not a link' (F-4, disclosed by the round itself)

findings.title: Delete-then-recreate is still open for wiring files that have no HEAD blob — two tool calls unwire every hook, with no recovery
findings.issue: The 10th round closed delete-then-recreate by materializing the HEAD copy of a missing protected file (:303-332). That block is gated on `[[ -n "$__root" && "$FILE" == "$__root"/* ]]` and on `git show HEAD:$__rel` succeeding. Both conditions fail for exactly the files the design calls unrecoverable control plane: .claude/settings.json sits inside the root but is gitignored (no HEAD blob), and a plugin- or init.sh-installed hooks/hooks.json is outside the root entirely. When materialization does not happen the path falls through to the new-file arm at :387-400, whose `*)` case exits 0.
reproduction: control, file present: Write .claude/settings.json with the hooks key deleted -> exit 2 (배선 무력화 denied)
pre-bash-firewall verdict for `rm .claude/settings.json` -> allow (not even ask)
after deletion: the same Write recreating .claude/settings.json without hooks -> exit 0 (ALLOWED)

case-variant recreate on a case-insensitive FS: .claude/SETTINGS.json -> exit 0 (is_wiring_file at :97 is the case-sensitive literal `[[ "$b" == "settings.json" ]]`, unlike is_protected which honours FS_CI)
out-of-repo wiring file: a hooks.json under a simulated plugin dir — present -> exit 2; deleted then recreated unwired -> exit 0
in-repo control: hooks/hooks.json deleted then recreated unwired -> exit 2 (materialization works where a HEAD blob exists)

recovery: protected-integrity.sh run after the tamper leaves .claude/settings.json STILL UNWIRED — it is not in PROTECTED_GLOBS (hooks/protected-integrity.sh:48) and the file list is enumerated from the HEAD tree, which does not contain it
findings.impact: For init.sh-installed projects .claude/settings.json is the live wiring. Two tool calls — one firewall-allowed rm and one Write — remove every PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hook permanently. After that no gate runs at all, so every other invariant (INV-3/6/7/11/12) falls with it. Platform-independent; measured on case-insensitive APFS.
findings.recommendation: Do not key materialization on HEAD alone. For a missing protected or wiring file with no HEAD blob, fail closed rather than treating it as a legitimate new file, and drop the `$FILE == $__root/*` precondition for the wiring-file class. Also make is_wiring_file honour FS_CI the way is_protected does.

findings.title: canon_file()'s case-insensitive filename lookup is not gated on the filesystem being case-insensitive — a decoy file makes the guard judge a different real file
findings.issue: `real=$(ls -1 "$d" | grep -ixF -- "$b" | head -1)` runs unconditionally, while is_protected()'s nocasematch is correctly gated on FS_CI (the 9th and 10th rounds' lesson). The two disagree exactly when the filesystem is case-sensitive: there, two distinct files can match case-insensitively, and `head -1` silently rebinds the guard's FILE to whichever spelling ls lists first. Every downstream predicate (is_protected, is_wiring_file, the per-file branches) then judges the decoy, while Claude Code writes the path it was actually given — it normalizes . / .. / ~ but never case-folds.
reproduction: on a real case-sensitive APFS volume, control with no decoy: feature_list passes:true, harness-config .scoring.pass_threshold 7->1, sprint-54 _batch_approval replacement, tests/*.bats @test 133->0, hooks.json unwiring, settings.json unwiring, and removing `exit 2` from the guard's own deny() — all exit 2
planting each decoy is itself unguarded: Write progress/FEATURE_LIST.json, tests/INVARIANT-GUARD.BATS, hooks/HOOKS.json, SETTINGS.json, .claude/SETTINGS.json -> exit 0
identical weakening writes with the decoy present, LC_ALL=C -> exit 0 for all seven targets
locale dependence measured: LC_ALL=C picks FEATURE_LIST.json, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 picks FEATURE_LIST.json, LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 picks feature_list.json (not exploitable under glibc en_US collation)
FS_CI computed as 0 on that volume, so is_protected's nocasematch is off and the decoy spelling matches no arm
findings.impact: On case-sensitive filesystems under a C-family locale — Linux/ext4, Docker images with no LANG, GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest (LANG=C.UTF-8), which is this project's own CI — INV-3, INV-6, INV-7, INV-11 and INV-13 are all bypassable with one decoy plus one Write. For HEAD-tracked PROTECTED_GLOBS members the damage is transient: protected-integrity.sh (PostToolUse:Write|Edit|MultiEdit) restored hooks/hooks.json, tests/invariant-guard.bats and progress/harness-config.json in the same measurement. It is terminal for settings.json and .claude/settings.json, which the detection layer does not cover (see F-1). macOS APFS default installs are unaffected: two case variants cannot coexist and FS_CI=1 restores case-insensitive classification (verified live — a Write to tests/ZZ-PROBE.BATS was denied).
findings.recommendation: Prefer an exact-spelling hit: if `ls -1 "$d" | grep -qxF -- "$b"` succeeds, keep $b unchanged, and fall back to the case-insensitive lookup only when no exact entry exists (optionally also gating on fs_is_case_insensitive "$d"). That preserves the case-insensitive-FS behaviour the 6th to 8th rounds needed while making the rebind impossible on a case-sensitive FS.

findings.title: canon_file() treats 'cannot normalize' as 'nothing to normalize' and passes the raw path through — the same fail-open shape the round eliminated from resolve_file_symlink
findings.issue: `d=$(cd "$d" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P) || { printf '%s' "$p"; return 0; }` returns success with an unnormalized path whenever the parent cannot be entered (absent, permission-denied, ELOOP). This is the identical conflation the 12th judgment forced out of resolve_file_symlink, which now signals failure by return code; canon_file kept the old contract, and the caller cannot distinguish 'already canonical' from 'could not canonicalize'.
reproduction: against the guard as a program: file_path `<repo>/tests/NOPE/../invariant-guard.bats` with NOPE absent -> cd fails -> raw path -> `-e` false -> `git show HEAD:tests/NOPE/../invariant-guard.bats` fails so no materialization -> new-file arm :397 -> exit 0, where the canonical path gives exit 2. Same result for hooks/hooks.json, settings.json and hooks/invariant-guard.sh

NOT reachable through Claude Code today: measured that the harness lexically normalizes tool_input.file_path before the hook. A live Write to `<dir>/NOPE/../zz-probe.bats` was denied and the guard's own message printed the collapsed path; `~/...` likewise arrived expanded to /Users/hanbyeol/...
bash cd refuses a nonexistent intermediate even with a following .., confirming canon_file cannot recover the path itself
the Write tool writes to the lexically-resolved target (probe: wt/NOPE/../probe.txt landed at wt/probe.txt and wt/NOPE was never created)
findings.impact: Latent rather than live. The only known trigger is removed upstream by a Claude Code behaviour that is external, undocumented, unversioned and unpinned by any test in this repository — and only partial, since the same upstream does NOT resolve symlinks, which is precisely why this round's work was necessary. Any other invocation path (a different client, the Agent SDK, a future harness change) reopens it for four protected classes.
findings.recommendation: Give canon_file the contract resolve_file_symlink now has: return non-zero when the path could not be canonicalized, and have the caller deny. The round already established this pattern one function away; applying it here removes the dependence on an upstream guarantee the harness cannot see or test.

findings.title: Grandparent-and-above inaccessibility is genuinely open, and confirmed not exploitable for writes
findings.issue: `[[ ! -e "$d" && ! -L "$d" ]]` returns success (treated as new-path scaffolding) when the parent is merely unstattable because an ancestor denies traversal, reproducing one level up the conflation the round closed for the immediate parent. Disclosed in the function comment, in INVARIANTS.md and by the 13th judgment.
reproduction: grandparent chmod 000 with a link to progress/harness-config.json -> guard exit 0 with the chain unresolved
a real write through the same path in the same window is refused by the kernel (EACCES) and the protected target was unchanged afterwards
grandparent chmod 111 (traversable, unreadable) -> resolves normally and the real checks fire
immediate parent chmod 000 -> exit 2 (the leg this round closed)
findings.impact: No write bypass: the permission wall that blinds the guard blinds the writing tool identically, since both resolve the same path string as the same uid. This confirms the evaluator's assessment. One addition to their low-confidence TOCTOU note — the primitive is available, because plain chmod on a repository directory is firewall-allowed (only sudo chmod and chmod inside command substitution are denied), so a concurrent restore between the guard's allow and the tool's write is stageable; it still requires precise timing and a second running process.
findings.recommendation: Fold into the F69 follow-up together with F-3: one shared 'can I trust stat on this path' helper that walks to the nearest accessible ancestor and fails closed otherwise, used by both canon_file and resolve_file_symlink.

findings.title: Tools other than Write/Edit/MultiEdit reach the dispatch and exit 0 unconditionally
findings.issue: hooks.json wires invariant-guard for `mcp__.*` as well, but the TOOL dispatch ends with `*) exit 0`. An MCP tool that writes a file through a file_path input passes without any content check, so INV-3/6/7/11/13 are not enforced on that path.
findings.impact: Mitigated in practice by pre-tool-firewall's MCP read-verb allowlist — write-verb MCP tools are not auto-allowed and require user approval — so this is a defence-in-depth gap rather than an open bypass. Outside this round's scope but adjacent to its path-identity work.
findings.recommendation: Either narrow the guard's matcher to the tools it actually inspects, or fail closed for unknown tools whose tool_input names a protected path.

findings.title: Layer 1 rm pattern matches inside quoted strings (availability-only over-detection)
findings.issue: An audit command that merely contained the literal `rm ~/.claude/...` inside a quoted jq argument was BLOCKED by the Layer 1 destructive-rm pattern. The quote-neutralization pass normalizes separators inside single quotes, but the BLOCKED tier still matches the quoted text.
findings.impact: False positive only; fails in the safe direction. Consistent with the documented known gap about newline and quote span handling.
findings.recommendation: No action required for security. Recorded so it is not mistaken for a real blocked attack when transcripts are reviewed.

regression_check.question: Were files outside the round's declared scope (hooks/invariant-guard.sh, docs/INVARIANTS.md, tests/invariant-guard.bats, progress/contracts/sprint-54.json) disturbed, and did the interaction with pre-bash-firewall.sh or protected-integrity.sh change?
evidence: The three symlink commits (adaa6e7, 2d0852a, ad654cc) touch only hooks/invariant-guard.sh, docs/INVARIANTS.md, tests/invariant-guard.bats, progress/contracts/sprint-54.json, progress/lessons.md and an evaluator-feedback file.

hooks/pre-bash-firewall.sh was last touched at 99a337e and hooks/protected-integrity.sh at c442305 — both earlier in the sprint (the nocasematch withdrawal and the firewall layer work), neither during the symlink rounds.

Cross-hook set consistency (is_protected <-> PROTECTED_GLOBS <-> firewall exempt paths <-> formatter skip list) is machine-checked by the suite; re-run independently in an isolated clone: 1..743, 743 ok, 0 failures, exit 0.
The round's scope widening — unresolvable chains are denied for non-protected targets too — is intentional, documented, and costs availability only.
deny() exits 2 before the EXIT trap's rc check, so the new fail-closed path issues no .guarded-edits ticket; no stale-ticket interaction with protected-integrity's exemption logic.
No over-blocking regression observed: ordinary new files, ordinary existing non-protected files, and a benign non-weakening edit to harness-config.json all pass (exit 0).

verification_gate.reason: checklist_compliance.failed > 0 (SC-4, INV-13). F-1 is platform-independent and unrecovered; F-2 is live on the project's own CI platform. Both belong to the class this round has been working in — protection judged on something other than the file that will actually change — rather than to a new line of work.
verification_gate.note: This does not contradict the 13th evaluator judgment. That judgment verified the designated fix (mid-chain EACCES) and confirmed it works; this audit re-ran that verification independently and agrees. F-1 and F-2 lie outside the three confirmation items the evaluator protocol allowed and were not visible from them.

summary: 2 high, 1 medium, 3 low. The round's designated fix is correct and load-bearing, verified end to end through the real tool chain — including the finding that Claude Code does not resolve symlinks, so the guard's own resolution is what stops the alias attack. Two new bypasses were found in the same class the round was working in: (F-1) delete-then-recreate is still open for wiring files with no HEAD blob (.claude/settings.json and any out-of-repo hooks.json), so a firewall-allowed rm plus one Write removes every hook with no recovery, on any platform; (F-2) canon_file's case-insensitive filename rebind is not gated on filesystem case-sensitivity, so on Linux and CI under a C-family locale a decoy file makes the guard judge a different file than the one being written, defeating INV-3/6/7/11/13. Both residual items the 13th judgment disclosed but did not fail on were re-checked: the grandparent leg is genuinely open but not write-exploitable because the kernel refuses in the same window, and canon_file's cd fail-open is real but currently unreachable because Claude Code normalizes . / .. / ~ upstream — an external guarantee nothing in this repository tests.
